# Best Portable Power Stations for Camping

The right size depends on how you camp. For tent or car camping, you mostly charge phones, run lights, and maybe a CPAP, so a **250–500 Wh** unit is enough. If you want to run a 12V fridge or cook with electric appliances, you'll need about **1,000 Wh or more**.

## Light weekend trips (~300 Wh, under 10 lb)

| Pick | Capacity / Output | Weight | Price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | Lightest and simplest. Covers several nights of a CPAP with the humidifier off. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286 Wh / 600 W | ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 | Twice the inverter output. Expandable to 572 Wh. |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288 Wh / 300 W | ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in retractable lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the AC version, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268 Wh / 600 W | ~10.1 lb | ~$179 | Cheapest LiFePO4 option. |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Jackery has replaced the 300 Plus with the 300 v2 on its own site, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon.

## Mid-size: fridge, fans, small appliances (~1 kWh)

- **BLUETTI AC180**: 1,152 Wh LiFePO4, 1,800 W inverter, about 35 lb, 5-year warranty. It costs $499, or **$474.05 with code `AFF5OFF`**. The code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21.
  **[Buy the BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** ([details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
  This is an affiliate link from the deal site Dealectric. It goes to Bluetti's official US store, and the site earns a commission. You can also go directly to Bluetti's store and enter the same code. The AC180 has no expansion port.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It delivered 890 Wh of usable power in testing, weighs 25 lb, and is on sale for under $530 ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: TechRadar's camping pick, with easy solar pairing ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)).

## Multi-day off-grid or overlanding (1.5–2 kWh, ~39 lb)

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top off-grid camping pick. It delivered 1,710 Wh of usable power and is under $900 on Amazon ([source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65 weatherproof and drop-resistant, and costs about $1,079 on Amazon ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)).

## My recommendation

- **Most tent or car campers:** the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, or the EcoFlow River 3 Plus if you want more output.
- **You plan to run a fridge:** the Bluetti AC180 with the code above.
- **Week-long off-grid trips:** the Jackery 2000 v2.

The search results didn't include direct store links for the models other than the AC180. Searching the model name on Amazon or the brand's site will find them. Black Friday is about a month away, so prices may drop soon.
